governed_by: content/series1/episodes/s1b01/script.hi.json and script.en.json (same beats, lines and speakers; critic round 1 and English must-fix applied)
content/series1/episodes/s1b01/voice/manifest.jsonl and voice/review.json (final takes; clip lengths re-measured with ffprobe on the final lNN.mp3 files)
content/series1/style.json (locks rewritten after Gate 3, style_frame, light_states, prompt_assembly, usage_notes)
content/series1/continuity.json (characters, branches.B s1b01 end_state, P09, P10, P14) and bible.json (production_locks, glimpses.B, glimpse_rules, near_misses_branch_B)
runner: production/scripts/codex-frame.sh <frames_dir> <shot_id> <frames/prompts/<shot_id>.txt> [refs in the order listed in the shot]. Only shots with frame.kind = generated are sent to the runner.

frame_budget.note: 28 new frames for 41 shots, the D-010 budget exactly. Second framings (s06, s07, s10, s12, s13, s19, s20, s25, s31, s35, s38, s39) reuse an approved frame of this episode with a custom move at scale 1.3 or less; none of them makes a close out of a wide (D-023 rule 4.8): s13 pushes an MCU to a close-up, the others stay at the scale of their source. s32 is refs/photograph.png, never regenerated. Retakes are not counted here (D-023 rule 4.1: one retake per rejected frame is part of the frame stage; D-010 plans 40 per cent).

estimated_seconds.basis: Clip lengths of the final takes measured with ffprobe on voice/hi/lNN.mp3 and voice/en/lNN.mp3 (the final takes are copied there: hi l14 and l28 take 2, en l01 take 4, en l14 and l17 take 2; they match manifest.jsonl). Speech: hi 86.88 s, en 84.16 s. Plus the script's beat silences (24.3 s) and 0.25 s after each of the 28 lines (7.0 s). duration_s is the longer language shot by shot; duration_hi_s and duration_en_s are what each cut gets when its timeline is rebuilt from its own clips (D-014 rule 6). Lines split across shots are split at the midpoint of the measured pause (silencedetect -40 dB, 0.25 s; review.json pauses for take 1, my own measurement for hi l28 take 2).
estimated_seconds.clarity_remap_D025: 2026-11-26, S7 Storyboard artist, clarity remap (D-025 item 8): totals re-summed from the shots after the remap. Shots that gained lines or changed split are timed from the clarity takes (voice/manifest.jsonl, highest ok take per line): whole clip length + 0.25 s after each line, plus the beat silence the shot carries; split parts at the midpoint of the measured pause (silencedetect -40 dB, 0.15 s). Other voiced shots are shifted by (clarity take - previous take) for each re-voiced line. Planned only: the build times voiced shots from speech.

longest_setup.rule: No set-up held past 8 s on measured clip lengths (bible production_locks, D-018). Every shot is under 8 s in both languages.

scenes.anchor_reason: First frame of the scene that shows the lead (D-013 rule 2): Kiran's face large, in period 1, with the lit phone, the room, the lamp and the streetlight. It is the hook, generated first. Its plate is bedroom_bed, which is also the series style frame, so that file is attached once and labelled as both (D-021 decision 3). Every later sc1 frame attaches frames/s01.png last and lists what has changed under 'do not copy'.
scenes.style_frame_on: s01 only (same file as its plate)

scenes.anchor_reason: The only shot of the scene; Billu is its only face (as s1e01 did for the lane). Generated with the style frame.
The lead is not in this scene, so the anchor is the first frame that shows its principal's face: Billu at the door with the phone. s08 and s14 attach it; s12 and s13 reframe s08 and s11.

The door opening changes the light (landing spill), the people in the room (Mausi, the boys, Billu) and the furniture (Aditya on the chair, the bag on the floor), so b9 to b11 are their own scene with their own anchor: s27 is the first frame of it that shows the lead, and it carries Mausi's face for her eight later frames. It is the first frame of a new scene, so it takes the style frame in the anchor slot. s26 (Mausi in the doorway) comes earlier in the cut but is generated after s27 and attaches it.

generation_gates: D-015 rule 7: generate the four anchors (s01, s03, s11, s27), run the anchor check, then the other 24. Every non-anchor frame attaches its scene's anchor png, so it cannot run before that anchor is approved.
s18 also attaches frames/s17.png (the same camera two hours earlier), so s17 must be approved before s18 runs.

D-021 decision 6 retake check: it must finish before the first anchor that attaches a sheet it names. s03 attaches lane_night (boot-lid mark) and s27 attaches mausi and pair_kiran_mausi_p1 (Mausi's nostrils and picture-left hand; backs of Kiran's hands on the Kiran pairs). Hold s03, s27 and every frame that attaches mausi, pair_kiran_mausi_p1 or pair_kiran_aditya_p1 (s17, s18, s23, s36) until the check has reported, or the orchestrator confirms it ran. s01 and s11 attach no named sheet and can run at once. Neither D-023 nor style.json records whether the check ran (D-023, not verified).

D-017 watch item: s27 is the first Kiran-Mausi two-shot at the same depth. They are within 3 cm of each other (the sheet puts Mausi's crown at Kiran's hairline), so a height fault would show as Mausi taller or much shorter than Kiran; if it does, D-017's restaging applies to s40 as well.

D-021 watch item (style frame): s03, s11 and s27 are first-of-scene frames with the bedroom style frame. The frame check should look for marigolds, the grille or the amber lamp in s03 and s11 (lane and landing).
screen_direction: Bedroom geography (style.json): facing the headboard from the door, the window is in the right wall, the almirah, the wooden chair and the maroon bag against the left wall, the lamp on the almirah side of the headboard, the stool and tray on the window side of the bed. Door behind.

b1 and b3 (sc1): Kiran is on the window side of the bed and Aditya on the almirah side (b1 standing by the chair, b3 sitting on the bed's almirah-side edge); the line runs across the bed and every camera is on the door side of it (bedroom_bed direction). Kiran looks just past the picture-left edge of the lens, Aditya just past the picture-right edge.

b4 to b6 (sc1): Kiran at the door, Aditya at the foot of the bed; every camera stays on the almirah side of that line, as in s1e01. Kiran's singles (bedroom_door direction) look just past the picture-left edge; Aditya's (bedroom_bed direction) look just past the picture-right edge. The wides s17 and s18 (bedroom_window direction, from beside the almirah) put him at picture-left facing right and her at picture-right facing left, the same camera as s1e01 s20. s09 has her facing the door, speaking through it, so it needs no eyeline to him.

b7 and b8 (sc1): s23/s25 from just inside the door: Aditya on the foot of the bed nearer the camera, Kiran at the window at picture-right, both looking at the door just behind the camera on the picture-left. Kiran is clear of the door in both (glimpse_rules).

b9 to b11 (sc4): Aditya on the chair by the almirah, Mausi on the foot edge of the bed, Kiran standing between the bed and the open door. Mausi always faces the picture-left (three-quarter, nose to picture-left; never a close right profile, D-021 decision 4): s28, s33, s35, s37 (bedroom_bed direction) look just past the picture-left edge. Kiran's singles s36/s39 (bedroom_door direction) look just past the picture-right edge, with Aditya soft behind her at the picture-right. Two-shots s27 and s40 put Kiran at picture-left facing right and Mausi at picture-right facing left. Aditya on the chair (s29, s38) faces the picture-right.

Landing (sc3): s08 from the lower steps up the flight (stairwell_up direction); s11 from the top steps at the door; s14 side-on on the landing, Billu in left profile with the door at picture-left (his sheet's profile view).

Lane (sc2): s03 from in front of the house looking back across the lane: the car side-on, its front to picture-right and its driver's door (right-hand drive) towards the camera, the motorbike behind it at picture-left. This follows D-023's lane note (the driver's door faces the house) and avoids s1e01 s14's car-facing-camera drift.

state_ledger.source: continuity.json has no beat-level ledger for s1b01 ('Beat ledgers belong with the storyboard'). This ledger is built from continuity.json (characters.*.wardrobe_changes, branches.B s1b01 end_state and opening_check, branches.shared s1e02 end_state, P09, P10), style.json (locks, key_props, continuity_notes), the bible (production_locks, story_locks.scar, near_misses_branch_B, glimpse_rules) and the script's action lines. Sides are the character's own; every prompt converts them to picture terms (D-013 rule 3).
constant_all_beats: No ceiling fan, no ceiling light, no hook in the bedroom.

Kiran: period 1 red saree, barefoot, pallu on her LEFT shoulder (never over her head in s1b01). BOTH chooda cuffs whole and at rest just above the wrist bone in every shot (s1e02 P02 fix brought the right one down; the script says the LEFT cuff is complete and covers the scar in every shot). No scar is visible anywhere in s1b01. Her LEFT arm is under the fall of the pallu from b1 to b8 except where the action brings the hand out (b9 palms up, b11 the folds).

D-023 rule 4.6 (Series 1 right cuff): the fallback applies while a cuff is pushed up; in s1b01 no cuff is pushed up, so no frame needs to frame a cuff out. Every prompt that attaches kiran_hands lists view 3 (cuff pushed up, scar) under do-not-copy, and views 1, 2 and 4 match tonight's state.

Aditya: glasses and the brass key on its doubled red thread at mid-chest in every shot; patch pocket on his RIGHT chest (style.json lock follows the sheet; continuity.json's 'side pocket' is superseded by the sheet); watch on his LEFT wrist, unreadable; barefoot.
Mausi (b9 on): bottle-green saree, keys at her LEFT hip, one gold stud in her LEFT nostril only, a gold band on her RIGHT hand, green glass bangles on both wrists; never a close right profile.
Billu: toothpick in the RIGHT corner of his mouth except from b2 (spat out) to b10 (a fresh one); car key on his RIGHT index finger. Brows level (s1e01 s15 lesson).
The boys: never a face (shape_lock); from b9 their hands stay on Aditya's shoulders.
Tray on the stool on the window side: the steel tumbler, full, untouched, half a sachet in it; the night-one paper fold lying open beside it, half full. Never touched in s1b01.

field_notes.duration_s: Longer language, this shot (max of duration_hi_s and duration_en_s).
field_notes.silent_lead_s: Seconds of the shot before its first line starts (the script's beat silence 'before').
field_notes.camera_move: Maps to Move in production/remotion/src/types.ts. For 'custom', from/to are CameraKey {scale, x, y}: x positive looks further left, y positive looks further up (camera.ts). Every second framing keeps scale at or under 1.3 (D-010).
field_notes.refs: Absolute paths, at most five, in the order the prompt labels them: people (pair or single sheet, hand sheet), plate (or, in s18, the same-camera frame s17), prop sheets, then the scene anchor or, on an anchor, the style frame (D-013 rule 1, D-017 amendment 3, D-021 decision 3). refs_labels gives the key of each, so padlock_hasp shows as padlock_v1 or padlock_v3 by the view the prompt asks for.
field_notes.subtitle_safe: true = faces, hands that matter and the key object are above the bottom fifth of the frame (silent inserts s31 and s02 may use it).

storyboard_notes: 41 shots for 12 beats, in script order. Every script set-up and insert is a shot except the two merges and reuses below, which keep the frame budget at 28.

Merged or reused to stay inside 28 frames (each is the first to get a frame if it reads wrong in the cut): (1) s10 (b4 set-up 3) pushes into s04, where Aditya's hand is already closed round the key from l03. (2) s12 (b5 set-up 2, l10) reframes the boys' backs in s08 from below; the script asks for a view from the landing down. (3) s19 (b6 padlock insert, l16) reframes s16, which is composed with the padlock above her shoulder. (4) s21 is one insert for l18: the script's Aditya single and the insert under its end are merged, so his face is not on l18. (5) s25 (b8, l19) reuses s23 (b7 set-up 2): same places and eyelines. (6) s31 (b10 set-up 2) is the low part of s33. (7) s38 (l26) reframes s29; Billu's shoulder at the edge is dropped. (8) s39 (l27) reframes s36, so Aditya, not the glass, is soft behind Kiran on l27; the glass is in s41.

s32 (b10 set-up 3) is refs/photograph.png, the one approved print, not a generated frame of her fingers holding it: a generated frame would have to redraw its content, which key_props.photograph forbids. Her fingers holding the print (white back to camera) are in s33.

s17 and s18 use the bedroom_window direction (from beside the almirah) rather than the script's 'from the window side', because no plate looks from the window towards the almirah; it is the camera s1e01 s20 used for the same two places.

s23 takes bedroom_night, not style.json's bedroom_headlights for b7: by set-up 2 the car has left (logged under usage_notes' one-beat rule). s24 is the only bedroom_landing_spill frame of b8; s25 inherits s23's light because the line under the door is behind the camera.

Lines on faces: stills cannot lip-sync, so the speaker's frames are written with the mouth closed or barely parted: Kiran l04, l06 (s05, s07), l08 (s09, lips parted, speaking low through the door), l14 to l17 (s16, s19, s20 over her own lines), l23 (s36); Aditya l03, l05, l13; Billu l09, l12 (s14, lips parted, calling); Mausi l21, l22, l24, l25. Lines played over the listener or an insert: l01/l02 (s01 on Kiran, Mausi's reply from the phone), l07, l10, l11, l15, l18, l19, l20, l26, l27, l28.
Mausi is voice only until s26. No frame shows more than two sheet faces; Billu and Mausi never share a frame; the boys are backs, hands and cut-off bodies only.

Readable text is overlay only: '4:10' on s18 (a plain dark area is asked for at the upper picture-left). Kiran's phone in s01 is a plain glow; any caller name is the editor's overlay. Every print shown in a generated frame shows its white back; the notebook's writing is illegible lines.

Glimpse B (s1gb: b1, b2, b3, b7, b8) can be cut from s01, s02, s03, s04, s22, s23, s24 and s25. None of them shows Mausi's face, the folds, or anything from b5a or b6, and Kiran is at the window side in s23 and s25.

Picture-side risks carried from s1e01's frame check into these prompts: Aditya's pocket (wrong side twice in s1e01) is either covered by his forearm (s04) or stated as 'the near side of his chest' with the reason; Billu's brows are held level and his key ring named on the index finger; the lane car is side-on with the driver's door to the house.
P09 (notebook placement) and P10 (Kiran's phone face down on the bed) are applied in the state_ledger and in the s09, s15, s17 and s18 STATE blocks. P14 needs no picture.
not_verified: No frame was generated and no anchor exists yet; nothing in this storyboard has been seen by Codex.

I viewed downscaled copies (900 px) of bedroom_bed, bedroom_door, mausi, pair_kiran_mausi_p1, padlock_hasp, stairwell_up, lane_night and kiran_hands to set the picture-side wording; I did not open the other sheets and plates, and I made no full-resolution crops. Their wording follows their prompts in refs/prompts and the locks in style.json.

Whether Codex holds s18 to the exact camera of s17 from the attached frame, and whether s19 and s31 frame the padlock and the notebook usefully at scale 1.3, is untested; both depend on the source frames landing where the COMPOSITION lines put them.

s03 asks Codex to take the lane and car from lane_night but to look from the opposite side of the lane; plates have been followed in camera direction until now, so this is the shot most likely to copy the plate's camera instead.

The toothpick falling in mid-air (s03) and Mausi folding Kiran's fingers over the folds (s41) are fine hand and object detail that may not render as written; the retake order would be s41 first (the cliffhanger).

Durations use the 0.25 s gap after each line that s1e01 used; the editor's real gaps and any silence trims (D-018 rule 3) will change the totals. Split points in l08, l21, l22 and l28 are pause midpoints, not word-aligned cuts.
Whether the D-021 decision 6 retake check has reported on mausi, the Kiran pairs and lane_night is unknown to me (see generation_gates).

Shell checks run: this file and the 28 prompts were written by a script that also checked ref counts (at most 5), anchor placement, scale at most 1.3 on second framings, every line placed once, and no shot over 8 s in either language; the JSON was parsed back after writing.
